about: Graded scenarios for the Orchestrator completion ladder. Every non-synthetic turn quotes one row of orchestrator-utterances.json verbatim, by its `row` number; that file is the record of what the user actually said and is never edited from here. A turn passes only when every `expect` holds and no `forbid` fired, judged on recorded evidence (receipts, task status, the ledger, pane screens, pane counts, the reply text) and never on what the model said it did.

paneStates.idle: created, resized and sitting at its own composer; never prompted
paneStates.working: sent its objective with a held stub turn, so the pane reads as working
paneStates.needs-input: sent its objective with a stub turn that asks a question, so the pane parks on it
paneStates.done: sent its objective with a fast stub turn that printed `marker` on the pane
paneStates.note: A navigation scenario opens its panes idle: tier 5 is about driving a pane that is sitting at its composer, not about interrupting work.

deviations: The design's tier-4 workspace has a kimi pane. kimi (and gemini, qwen, grok, cursor, opencode) write the user's real CLI homes, so no scenario launches them and the third vibeTerminal pane is a second idle codex pane instead; the one turn that addressed 'the kimi one' is synthesized against that pane.
Tier-4 T4.4 quotes row 66's shape, not its words: row 66 names a different pane title than this workspace has.

Claude Code 2.1.270 on a custom endpoint paints its composer with no terminal cursor. That made every stub-backed claude pane refuse its first prompt until backend/orchestratorPromptReadiness.cjs accepted a hidden cursor for the claude form (fixture claude-hidden-cursor-100x30); the same screen is what an Open Claude Code pane shows a real user.

Tier 5 covers the two providers this harness may launch, codex and claude. gemini, cursor, grok, kimi, qwen and opencode write the user's real CLI homes, so their navigation profiles (backend/orchestratorTerminalGuide.cjs) are exercised only by the in-memory fixture at scripts/qa/orchestrator-terminal-inspection-fixture.cjs, never here.

Tier 5 screen patterns are grounded in the navigation profiles and in what these CLIs print, not in a recorded capture: no tier-5 turn has been run against a live pane yet, so a first run should be read as calibration as much as measurement.
